type_system_comparison.label: type_system_comparison
type_system_comparison.description: Type system snapshot across languages used in this atlas.
type_system_comparison.adapterInsight: Use this as a context switch cheat: nominal vs structural typing, and static vs dynamic guarantees, changes how you design APIs and tests.

codes.python:
# Python: dynamic duck typing (hints are optional)
def twice(x):
    return x * 2           # works for int, str, list, ...
name: str = "Ada"        # type hint for tools, not hard runtime enforcement
codes.scala3:
// Scala 3: static strong typing with givens/using
val n = 2                  // inferred Int
trait Show[T]:
  def show(v: T): String
given Show[Int] with
  def show(v: Int): String = v.toString

project_lifecycle.label: project_lifecycle
project_lifecycle.description: Project structure, build system, and main entry points across languages.
project_lifecycle.adapterInsight: Every language has a different philosophy: C++ is modular; Go is simplicity; Python is flexibility; TypeScript mirrors Node conventions; Scala bridges JVM tooling.

codes.python:
# pyproject.toml (modern PEP 517)
[project]
name = "my_app"
version = "0.1.0"

# main.py
if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("Hello")

# Run: python main.py

collection_mappings.label: collection_mappings
collection_mappings.description: Equivalent collection types across languages: the Rosetta Stone for data structures.
collection_mappings.adapterInsight: Use this table to quickly find the right data structure in your target language. Performance characteristics vary: dynamic arrays are fast for append; linked lists are fast for insertion; hash maps prioritize lookup speed.

codes.python:
# Common patterns
v = [1, 2, 3]
m = {"a": 1}
s = {3, 1, 2}
from collections import deque
q = deque([1, 2, 3])
arr = (1, 2, 3)  # immutable
codes.scala2:
// Common patterns
val v = Vector(1, 2, 3)
val m = Map("a" -> 1)
val s = Set(3, 1, 2)
val l = List(1, 2, 3)
val q = scala.collection.immutable.Queue(1, 2, 3)
